title: TPL tooling config
description: Reference data consumed by tpl:* commands. Looked up as tpl.config.json at the directory where the commands are invoked, or passed explicitly via --config (so a shared file such as adr.config.json can be reused).

idFormat.description: TPL id / filename convention. `date-sequence` expects `TPL-YYYYMMDD-NN-<slug>.md` (id `TPL-YYYYMMDD-NN`); `issue-number` expects `TPL-<n>-<slug>.md` (id `TPL-<n>`, no zero padding).

topics.description: Controlled vocabulary for a TPL's `topic` field. Empty or omitted disables topic validation.

indexFile.description: Generated index file, relative to the TPL directory and inside it, with `/` separators (no backslash, no leading or trailing `/`, no `..`), and not named `TPL-*.md` directly in it, which would be read as a TPL (e.g. `index.md`). When set, `tpl regenerate` writes it, grouped by topic, and `tpl validate` checks it instead of README.md. Omit to keep a hand-maintained README index.

checklistHeading.description: Heading text of the checklist section, without `#` (e.g. `Checklist`). When set, each checklist item may end with `[guard: `path`]` (enforced by the named file) or `[judgment]` (not decidable by a program); `tpl validate` requires the section, at least one item, and well-formed markers, and needs `--source-prefix` to check guard paths; `tpl regenerate`, `tpl related --status`, `tpl checklist` and `tpl review-body` show the enforcement status derived from the markers. Omit to turn all of this off.
